text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ontario cuts pollution funds: Memo reveals government wants private sector to finance Great Lakes cleanup plans.
- C$97,000 nets zero in entry scheme: Latest twist in immigrant plan.
- Bucaram resigns as Ecuador's president: Victim of 'congressional coup,' ousted leader vows to run in next election.
- Celestial looking glasses: bane or boon?
- Jan Brown wants to tackle Manning for Tories: Former star of Reform says Calgarians will love her plan to challenge leader of her old party.
- Canadian 88 scraps takeover: Hostile pursuit of Morrison Petroleums 'definitely' won't be repeated, president says.
- G7 satisfied with recovery of U.S. dollar: Finance leaders say 'misalignments' in exchange markets corrected.
- Bell, Telus to defend cable TV market trials.
- Murray Frum nabs power hitter as he pitches to win Blue Jays.

- Shakeup in dairy sector: Two big deals come back to back. Ault plans sale of Ontario unit to Agropur while an unnamed buyer, probably Italy's Parmalat, pays C$290 million to Beatrice. ((Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100)) (c) Reuters Limited 1997
